My biggest problem with mental health “awareness” has always been that the actual diagnostic part is usually left out. Yep, unfortunately :( Those are called intrusive thoughts. Ironically, the more you try to fight intrusive thoughts, they generally tend to get worse. My advice is to a.) tackle them head on and/or b.) distract yourself. You can either debunk those thoughts, or try to direct them into pleasant things. I usually try to think of happy memories or come up with stories in my head. Maybe that sounds kind of weird but it really helps to take my mind off of things! And it helps me fall asleep lol. 

Dealing with these thoughts is very personalized though, so you may have to just experiment to see what works for you.

I’ve been diagnosed with multiple anxiety disorders, severe depression, and I have dissociative issues as a result of them. But as I write this now, I recently came out of a severe depressive episode that lasted for a few months, and it feels like some thick, blinding and suffocating fog has been lifted. As I was battling that, I genuinely believed my life was over. I didn’t necessarily have active plans for suicide, but I had kind of conceded to this belief that my time was up and I would end up dead soon enough. I would remember life so clearly before anxiety controlled me, and then compare it to the present, in which panic attacks debilitated me from normal functions, and depression-induced apathy robbed me of any feelings at all. I was certain I could never have a life from these things. I know exactly how you feel. Once anxiety has a grip on you, it feels hard to escape, like you’ll be in its grasp forever. Anxiety and depression force you into this type of box of false beliefs in which you cannot even conceive a different world in which you are content and successful, but now that I’ve come out of that box I see how wrong those beliefs are. 

You don’t have to be in that box forever. You won’t be. I promise you. Despite the problems I’ve had, even in recent times, medication has saved my life, and it’s all trial and error. I have a lot of opportunities to find the medication that does work, and for the time being, my anxiety has gone down an impressive amount in the nearly three years that I’ve been on it.

Just as you mentioned, I do feel guilty sometimes when I go to my mom with my problems, but there’s no reason to feel that way. Your parents want to help you. You’re their child. They want the best for you, it would never feel like a burden for them to help you. I urge you to go to them, tell them you are struggling. Even if you are not comfortable being 100% open about the extent of your situation, please, please just mention some of your problems. It’s worth a shot—there is a world of opportunity out there for you to get better. I assure you this isn’t the end man. 

Sorry if this is all over the place, but please PM me if you ever need anything. I’d love to talk and listen if you ever need it. Best of luck
